flagship_directive: Prove a matching upper and lower bound for the rough regime \(0<t\le d/2\), \(0<s\le1/2\), uniformly over the bounded-density class, either establishing δ_n^\star\asymp\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}} or replacing that candidate with a rigorously matched primitive occupancy functional.
critique: The note proves a density-robust root-rate upper bound for \(t>d/2\), with the matching converse only under an explicit nondegenerate quadratic-mean-differentiable path, and proves a slower all-tests lower bound for uniform design when \(t<d/2\) and \(0<s\le1/2\). It does not deliver the advertised rough arbitrary-density frontier: there is no matching upper bound, and the proposed occupancy radius remains conjectural. The spectral optimality iff and adaptive regularization-grid test are only construction handles and open questions, so the title's spectral-frontier program is substantially broader than the proved results. The class-oracle constant \(V_\star\) is not computable from data, leaving no implementable size calibration or completed 401(k) analysis; these omissions constrain the leading-journal score despite the proved high-smoothness rate and rough-regime converse.
